inputs.title: The Thing
inputs.logline: When Bo cannot make himself leave home for the Learning Circle, Keen and Aida help him discover that the very tail he wants to hide might be the thing that helps him belong.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen turns a honeycomb into a private dare, trying to prove he can out-sneak a sleeping Fuzzby. The comedy is all body and sound: exaggerated quiet steps, betraying crunches, Fuzzby’s oblivious snore bubbles, and Keen inching closer because the prize keeps overriding caution.
beats.want: Keen wants to reach the honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that daring is not the same as being ready; his body will tell the truth before his pride does.
beats.kidRead: Sneaky steps, loud crunches, sleeping bee bubbles and the delicious suspense of almost getting caught.
beats.adultRead: A child testing boundaries while pretending he is in control, with every tiny noise exposing how not-in-control he is.
beats.emotionalIntent: Playful tension; make the audience lean forward and giggle before the sneeze release.

beats.need: She needs to trust quiet attention rather than force an answer.
beats.kidRead: Magic pink light shows a squirrel who cannot decide whether to pack or unpack.
beats.adultRead: The repeated satchel action is a familiar pre-departure spiral: doing tasks to avoid the door.
beats.emotionalIntent: Mystery, tenderness and focus; the audience should feel the pace hush.

beats.storyBeat: Inside his cozy hollow, Bo performs delay as routine: satchel, conker, answer Mum, and bargain for more time. The conker is his comfort object, and the door is already the real obstacle.
beats.want: Bo wants to postpone leaving while appearing as if he is almost ready.
beats.need: He needs someone to see that the delay is worry, not laziness.
beats.kidRead: Bo keeps getting ready but not going, and talks to his conker like a tiny ally.
beats.adultRead: A child’s avoidance loop made physical through packing rituals and a parent’s ordinary offscreen nudge.
beats.emotionalIntent: Domestic, recognisable and lightly comic, with worry under the warmth.

direction.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo bring the part of himself he cannot control into a new group and discover that it is welcome there?
direction.theme: Belonging begins when you stop hiding the part of you that feels too much.
direction.externalJourney: Keen is pulled from a playful honeycomb challenge into Aida’s errand, finds Bo stuck at his doorway, walks him through the Whispering Woods, and helps him arrive at the Learning Circle, where Bo’s tail becomes the day’s favourite game.
direction.internalJourney: Bo moves from packing and unpacking as a way to avoid the unknown, to letting one new friend see his tail, then letting a whole circle celebrate it.
direction.relationshipChanges: Bo and Keen begin as stranger and helper, become co-conspirators in a tail game, and end as real friends. Aida shifts from distant seer to gentle companion, using her own admission of repeated courage to make Bo feel less alone. The bears receive Bo not by fixing him, but by asking for more of what he feared would make them reject him.
direction.emotionalCurve: Bright comic mischief opens the episode, then narrows into Bo’s doorway dread. Warmth enters through Keen’s impressed reaction, dips again on the forest log, turns on Aida’s quiet honesty and the held wind beat, then lifts into shared light, group laughter, and a sunset button that keeps the honeycomb rivalry alive.

Aida’s vision of Bo packing and unpacking is paid off by Bo admitting four attempts and later walking out with the satchel. Bo’s feared tail “Thing” becomes first Keen’s admiration, then a forest game, then the Learning Circle’s delight. Aida’s “every single time” becomes Bo’s courage phrase as he steps forward. northStar.surfaceStory: Keen tries to sneak honey from Fuzzby’s honeycomb without waking him, but every tiny sound and sneeze betrays him.
northStar.universalTruth: A child can mistake boldness for readiness; the body often tells the truth before pride admits it.
northStar.childClearWant: Keen wants the honey and wants to prove he can be sneakier than a sleeping bee.
northStar.emotionalNeed: Keen needs to feel the difference between a fun dare and real control without being shamed for wanting to try.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If I keep acting brave and quiet enough, I can beat the challenge even when everything around me says I am not ready.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Fuzzby’s sleepy possessiveness turns the honey into a personal contest, and Zenny’s calm witnessing turns Keen’s failed sneak into a shared joke instead of a defeat.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: This is the kid reaching for the biscuit jar while insisting they are being silent, even as the chair squeaks, the packet rustles, and everyone already knows.
northStar.sceneTurn: The tiny pollen speck defeats all of Keen’s control: the private dare becomes public the instant the sneeze blows his cover.
audienceJourney: Leaning in as each crunch and snore bubble threatens discovery.
Released by the sneeze and Fuzzby’s half-awake authority.
Left amused that Keen has not learned the full lesson yet; he has only found a bigger challenge.
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: Playful, lightly suspenseful, and warmed by the sense that the contest will continue rather than truly hurt anyone.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: No extra explanation is needed. Keen’s lip lick, frozen paws, held sneeze and walk-away confidence carry the want; Fuzzby’s sleepy guard-dog posture carries the boundary; Zenny’s wink and hum carry the shared joke. Do not add lines that name embarrassment, temptation, bravery or failure.
northStar.environmentPressure: The Buzzing Nook actively betrays stealth: crunchy ground underfoot, pollen drifting into Keen’s nose, snore bubbles acting like ticking alarms, and the honeycomb sitting close enough to tempt him but guarded enough to make every inch dangerous.

tapestry.physicalMotif: Approach and recoil: Keen’s paw reaching toward honey, freezing back at crunches and pops, then finally being thrown out of hiding by the sneeze. The honeycomb remains the fixed prize; the snore bubbles and pollen are tiny moving gates that keep denying him.
tapestry.sonicMotif: Small sounds become enormous: CRUNCH, Fuzzby’s soft “ZZZZZ …”, bubble POPs, the held breath before “ACHOO!”, then Zenny’s steady “OHHMMMMM…” returning the nook to calm.

beats.emotionalIntent: Playful tension; make the audience lean forward and giggle before the sneeze release.

treatments.name: The Nook Is a Loud Little Trap
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience feels like they are sneaking with Keen through a place that refuses to be quiet. Every dew drop, dry leaf, snore bubble and pollen speck becomes enormous because Keen is treating this tiny honey mission like a heroic test. Children lean forward waiting for the next CRUNCH or POP; adults recognize the biscuit-jar child who thinks nobody can hear them.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Keen owns the scene emotionally. His want is simple and delicious: reach the honey. His need sits underneath: his body is already telling him he is not as ready or controlled as he wants to believe. Fuzzby is not an enemy; he is a sleepy boundary. Zenny is the calm witness who makes the failure safe by finding it funny without shaming him.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Escalating overcommitment plus environmental participation. Keen’s stealth becomes funnier because he performs quietness more and more intensely while the Buzzing Nook keeps answering with CRUNCH, POP and pollen. The smallest possible things defeat the biggest possible concentration. The sneeze is the release the scene has been winding toward from the first careful step.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Keen moves as if he has invented professional sneaking: high knees, careful paw placement, frozen whole-body statues after each betrayal, then renewed confidence because the honey keeps winning over caution. Fuzzby sleeps with possessive authority even before he wakes; his snore bubbles are part of his guard duty. When awake, he must sound grand but remain sleep-heavy, defending the honeycomb and then collapsing back into snoring mid-victory. Zenny does almost nothing until the end; her one wink and hum tell us she has understood everything longer than anyone else.
treatments.visualGrammar: The world is scaled to Keen’s nervous senses. The honeycomb is always the fixed temptation, while the path to it feels crowded with tiny hazards: crunchy ground underpaw, pollen drifting through bright air, snore bubbles swelling like alarms. Warm morning light begins inviting and soft, then becomes pricklier and more specific around bubble shine and pollen glitter as Keen’s control tightens. The grammar is playful suspense, not danger.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like Keen’s accomplice at first, lowering into his stealth logic and discovering obstacles as he does. It does not wait safely for the gag; it lets the CRUNCH interrupt its confidence and lets POPs startle the frame’s attention back to Fuzzby. At the end, the camera’s allegiance quietly transfers to Zenny’s knowing calm, revealing that the whole private dare was never fully private.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Keen is all preparation, stop-start recoil and renewed approach. Fuzzby’s body is mostly asleep, but the snore bubbles move with comic authority, turning stillness into threat. Zenny’s stillness is saved for the final punctuation; after Keen’s busy failure and Fuzzby’s sleepy bluster, her calm wink feels like the room exhaling.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth carries temptation and risk: foreground plants and stems partially hide Keen’s approach, the honeycomb glows as the reachable prize, and Fuzzby’s sleeping presence sits on top of it like a living lock. Pollen must read as spatial, drifting between Keen and the honey rather than appearing as an abstract effect. The environment should feel actively complicit in exposing him.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Begin with slow, delicious tiptoe suspense. Each CRUNCH creates a freeze, then each recovery is a little more committed and less wise. The snore bubbles create a repeated countdown pattern, but the second bubble should not feel identical; Keen is closer, hungrier and more invested. The pollen beat tightens the rhythm into held-breath anticipation before the sneeze breaks everything open. Fuzzby’s speech then slows the scene into sleepy pomp, and Zenny restores calm with one final hum.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by new threat, changed knowledge or comic punctuation only. No automatic action/reaction coverage. The scene should often stay with Keen long enough for the audience to feel him choosing not to back away, then cut only when a sound, bubble, pollen drift or emotional ownership changes the scene’s meaning. The final reveal of Zenny earns a new visual idea: the witness who has been outside Keen’s private fantasy all along.
treatments.openingImage: Golden morning dew and wildflowers frame the honeycomb on the stump as an irresistible prize; Keen’s lifted paw enters the world already mid-tiptoe, body pitched into a secret mission rather than posed at rest.
treatments.closingImage: The honeycomb remains untouched in warm calm while Zenny’s wink and “OHHMMMMM…” settle over the nook; Keen has lost the honey but kept the game, and the prize now feels like part of a friendship ritual.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make this a tidy sneaking master with safe inserts of feet, honey and reactions. The image must make tiny sounds feel physically huge without losing geography. I want the camera to be brave enough to be surprised by the nook — stems can occlude, pollen can pass close to lens, Fuzzby can dominate depth while asleep — but every four-year-old must still understand where Keen is, where the honey is, and why each inch closer is a worse idea.

treatments.name: The Honeycomb Is the Center of Gravity
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience experiences the honeycomb as the scene’s silent boss. Keen, Fuzzby, snore bubbles, pollen and Zenny all orbit it. The fun is not just whether Keen gets caught, but how the object keeps changing meaning: prize, dare, guarded treasure, forbidden trophy, then unfinished game.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The scene’s emotional point of view is split between Keen’s hunger for the dare and the honeycomb’s magnetic pull. Keen thinks he is choosing to sneak; the staging tells us the honey is choosing his next mistake. Fuzzby’s sleepy possessiveness turns the object into a boundary. Zenny’s final presence reframes it as a harmless shared joke rather than a real theft or defeat.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Anticipation to reversal, built around object desire. Every time Keen appears to gain control, the honeycomb’s world produces a new denial: crunching ground, snore-bubble alarm, another bubble, pollen, sneeze, Fuzzby’s sleepy proclamation. The reversal is never cruel; it simply proves that the dare is bigger than Keen’s current skill.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Keen’s acting should show appetite before strategy: eyes to honey, lip lick, paw reaching before his judgement catches up. His freezes are not generic fear; each one is the thought, “I can still save this.” Fuzzby, even asleep, must feel absurdly official about the honeycomb — his “ZZZZZ …” is a guard’s lullaby. When he says Keen is “never, ever, ever, ever, ever” going to get it, the performance is huge in intention but undercut by sleep. Zenny’s final hum lands as gentle audit: she has counted every mistake and still approves of the game.
treatments.visualGrammar: The composition keeps returning emotional weight to the honeycomb without repeating a fixed frame. The honey’s warmth should pull the eye through surrounding green and dew sparkle. The snore bubbles and pollen are moving punctuation around the central object. The world should feel like a small stage built by temptation: everything curves, points or drifts toward the honeycomb, then blocks Keen at the last moment.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is less Keen’s accomplice than a fascinated observer of attraction. It notices Keen being pulled closer, abandons him briefly when a bubble becomes more important, and lets the audience sometimes know a denial is coming before Keen does. That creates giggly dread: children can think, “Don’t do it!” while still wanting him to do it.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: The honeycomb is the still center. Keen’s approach-and-recoil pattern becomes a dance around it. Fuzzby’s sleeping stillness is unstable because his bubbles grow and pop. Zenny’s final stillness mirrors the honeycomb’s stillness: she belongs to the calm of the nook, not Keen’s frantic orbit.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Use circular depth around the stump: Keen’s path does not need to be a straight lane. He can pass through layered wildflowers, slip partly behind stems, reappear closer than expected, and then get stopped by a tiny airborne speck. The honeycomb should remain locatable as the center of the geography even when occluded for a breath. Environment is not background; it is the rules of the game.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The scene breathes in loops: desire, approach, tiny alarm, freeze, renewed desire. Each loop tightens the radius around the honeycomb. The second snore bubble should feel like the audience understands the rule and Keen foolishly believes he can beat it. The pollen interrupts the loop with something too small to plan for, forcing the sneeze release. Fuzzby’s half-awake speech is a victory lap that runs out of fuel, and Keen’s exit line reopens the loop for the future.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts should be object-motivated: the honeycomb’s pull, a bubble’s growth, pollen entering the danger zone, Fuzzby reclaiming possession, Zenny reframing the whole event. Avoid cutting merely because someone speaks. If the honeycomb’s meaning changes inside a held image, stay. If power over the honey shifts, cut decisively.
treatments.openingImage: The honeycomb sits in golden morning light on the stump, dew sparkling around it like it has summoned the whole nook; Keen’s careful approach is already visible as an orbit beginning around the prize.
treatments.closingImage: The same honeycomb remains in place, but now it is no longer just food — it is the undefeated center of Keen and Fuzzby’s playful contest, with Zenny’s calm hum folding the nook back around it.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: The danger is making the honeycomb a simple prop and covering the characters around it. I want the scene designed as gravitational staging: eye-lines, drifting pollen, bubble growth and Keen’s curved path all prove the honeycomb controls the space. Challenge any frame where the honeycomb is merely decorative or where Keen’s route becomes a flat left-right sneak. The geography can rotate; the object’s pull must stay readable.

treatments.name: Zenny Has Seen the Whole Movie
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience first believes they are inside Keen’s secret mission, then discovers the deeper joke: it was never secret. The final Zenny reveal retroactively makes the whole scene warmer. Children laugh because Keen got caught by sounds, bubbles and a sneeze; adults laugh because a calm witness has been letting a child have their harmless little dare.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Keen carries the active want, but Zenny quietly owns the scene’s wisdom. The emotional construction hides her point of view until the end. Keen needs to feel the failure without humiliation; Zenny’s witnessing gives him that. She does not stop him, scold him or solve anything. She simply lets the game be a game and seals it with “OHHMMMMM…”
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Concealment to revelation, with deadpan observation as the final punchline. Keen is concealing his noisy mission from Fuzzby, but the scene itself is concealing Zenny’s awareness from us. The sneeze exposes Keen to Fuzzby; the wink exposes the larger truth to the audience: calm has been watching chaos the whole time.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Keen plays absolute seriousness. He should never indicate he is being funny; his concentration is the joke. After the sneeze and Fuzzby’s warning, Keen’s recovery is important: he walks away amused, not crushed, because the dare has become even more interesting. Fuzzby’s waking is a comic flare-up of sleepy rank — a grand warning delivered by someone barely online — then he fades back into “ZZZZZ …” authority. Zenny’s performance is microscopic: a settled gaze, one wink, then the hum. No extra business. Her restraint is the release.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene uses selective awareness. Early frames favor what Keen notices: honey, ground, Fuzzby, bubbles. The edges of the nook may hold quiet negative space that later feels occupied by Zenny’s unseen attention. Light remains warm, but the final reveal should feel like the morning has been calm all along; only Keen experienced it as a thriller.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera pretends to be limited to Keen’s knowledge. It sneaks, startles and fixates with him. But it should occasionally leave just enough compositional calm in the world to make the final Zenny reveal feel earned, not random. When Zenny appears, the camera does not announce a twist with spectacle; it simply admits that a steadier point of view has been present outside Keen’s panic.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Keen’s motion is fussy, vertical, high-kneed and repeatedly arrested. Fuzzby is sleep-still except for bubbles, then briefly erupts into sleepy authority before collapsing back into rest. Zenny is withheld stillness: the scene saves true quiet until after the noise has spent itself. Her stillness does not compete with Keen’s action; it judges it kindly.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Early depth should create hiding places: flowers, stems and stump edges let Keen believe he has cover. Later, the same environment should reveal that hiding from Fuzzby is not the same as being unseen. Zenny can be discovered as part of the nook’s calm depth rather than introduced like a new arrival. The pollen must cross from environment into Keen’s body, making the nook the agent that blows his cover.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The first half is a hush game: tiptoe, CRUNCH, freeze; reach, POP, freeze; inch, second POP. The second half becomes bodily inevitability: pollen, held sneeze, “ACHOO!” Then comes the sleepy authority beat, with Fuzzby stretching “never” into absurd excess and dissolving into sleep. Keen’s “We’ll see, Fuzzby. We’ll see.” restores his pride playfully. Zenny’s “OHHMMMMM…” is the final downbeat, slower than everything before it.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: The edit should protect the delayed witness idea. Do not cut to Zenny early for easy reaction coverage. Let the audience live in Keen’s mistaken privacy until the moment when revealing Zenny changes the meaning of everything before it. Cuts before then belong to threat and exposure; the final cut belongs to changed point of view.
treatments.openingImage: Keen tiptoes into golden morning hush, knees lifted too high for someone trying to be invisible, while the honeycomb waits ahead and the nook feels like it is holding its breath with him.
treatments.closingImage: Zenny, calm and unhurried, gives one wink and hums “OHHMMMMM…” as the honeycomb sits untouched nearby; the scene ends on the kindness of being seen and not shamed.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: The obvious version cuts to Zenny as a reaction machine throughout, which kills the scene’s best reveal. I challenge us to stage her absence as presence: use depth, quiet space and sound restraint so the final wink feels inevitable in hindsight. Also resist safe symmetry between Keen and Fuzzby. The camera may believe Keen’s secrecy, but the frame should know the nook is wiser than he is.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: Combine: “The Nook Is a Loud Little Trap” governs, with “Zenny Has Seen the Whole Movie” as the closing reveal engine and “The Honeycomb Is the Center of Gravity” as the spatial discipline.
combinedFrom: The Nook Is a Loud Little Trap
Zenny Has Seen the Whole Movie
The Honeycomb Is the Center of Gravity
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience sneaks with Keen through a tiny golden nook that keeps loudly betraying him, then feels the warm relief that his failure has been witnessed kindly, not punished.
treatmentSelection.rationale: “The Nook Is a Loud Little Trap” is the best spine because it keeps the emotional ownership with Keen: his over-serious stealth, his appetite, his false belief that performance equals control, and his body finally telling the truth through the sneeze. It makes the environment an active comic partner rather than a backdrop, which gives the scene its originality and its kid-forward suspense. I want to graft in Treatment 3’s delayed Zenny awareness because it deepens the final beat: the joke is not only that Keen got caught, but that he was safe to be silly the whole time. I also want Treatment 2’s honeycomb gravity as a staging principle, not as the emotional lead: the honeycomb should organize space and desire, but Keen remains the heart. This combination gives us a clear rhythm — temptation, approach, tiny betrayal, renewed pride, bodily inevitability, sleepy boundary, kind witness — and preserves the co-viewing truth: children giggle at the noisy sneak; adults recognize the child being allowed to try, fail, and keep dignity.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: No selected element depends on fixed character lanes, keeping all characters visible, habitual action/reaction coverage, safe camera placement, repeated close-up punctuation, mechanical shot counts, generic “cinematic” language, or merely illustrating the script. I am not selecting Treatment 2 as the primary treatment because its pure version risks letting the honeycomb become the scene’s emotional owner; object gravity is useful, but the show’s meaning must stay in Keen’s pride meeting Zenny’s kind witness and Fuzzby’s sleepy boundary. I am not selecting Treatment 3 alone because its reveal structure is excellent but could over-privilege the delayed wink and underfeed the tactile suspense of CRUNCH, POP, pollen, and honey. Treatment 1 is therefore the governing treatment because it has the strongest playable suspense, clearest emotional ownership, best environmental pressure, and most flexible camera relationship.

scene.purpose: Open on Keen turning the honeycomb into a private stealth dare, let the Buzzing Nook loudly expose his overconfidence, then land the failure as a kind witnessed joke rather than a defeat.
scene.dramaticQuestion: Can Keen reach the honeycomb without waking Fuzzby, or will the tiny nook prove louder than his pride can control?
scene.connectionFromPreviousScene: This is the episode opening: golden morning temptation begins the story with play, appetite and a self-made challenge.
scene.handoverToNextScene: Keen leaves amused and challenged, with the untouched honeycomb and Zenny’s calm hum carrying the promise that wanting to prove oneself will continue into the episode.

beats.sourceScript: Keen turns a honeycomb into a private dare, trying to prove he can out-sneak a sleeping Fuzzby. The comedy is all body and sound: exaggerated quiet steps, betraying crunches, Fuzzby’s oblivious snore bubbles, and Keen inching closer because the prize keeps overriding caution.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.whatChanges: The honeycomb changes from an inviting prize into a guarded dare: every step announces Keen, Fuzzby’s sleeping presence becomes a living lock, and Keen’s appetite starts overriding his caution.
beats.whoDrives: Keen drives by choosing to keep advancing after each crunch and snore warning; the nook drives back through sound, texture and Fuzzby’s snore bubbles.
beats.audienceAnticipation: Children wait for the next tiny sound to betray him; adults recognize that he is much louder than he thinks and wait for the sleeping guard to notice.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen tiptoes with exaggerated high knees, freezes after the CRUNCHes, spots and reaches for the honey, then keeps reaching as Fuzzby snores and snore bubbles grow and pop near the prize.
beats.consequence: The approach becomes more dangerous and funnier without anyone attacking him: the environment has proven that his secret mission is already noisy.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The held stealth tension hands into an even smaller threat: if crunches and snore bubbles are this loud, a speck of pollen can become enormous.

emotionContract.entryState: Hungry, excited and proud of his private sneaking plan.
emotionContract.pressure: The honeycomb is close, Fuzzby is asleep on top of it, and every paw placement creates a betraying sound.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: He chooses to treat each betrayal as a pause, not a reason to quit; the honey keeps pulling him forward.
emotionContract.exitState: More invested and less sensible, with his body already proving that quiet control is fragile.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: High-kneed steps, repeated freezes after CRUNCHes, widened eyes, lip lick and a paw reaching closer despite Fuzzby’s snoring.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience knows the nook can hear him even if Keen keeps believing he can still win.

comedyContract.setup: A golden honeycomb sits within reach, and Keen enters already treating the trip toward it as professional stealth.
comedyContract.expectation: If he is careful enough, a sleeping Fuzzby will stay asleep and the honey will be his.
comedyContract.disruption: Each careful step answers with CRUNCH, and Fuzzby’s snore bubbles turn sleep itself into an alarm system.
comedyContract.button: Keen keeps reaching anyway, making the tiny nook look more in charge than the sneaking bear.
comedyContract.hold: Hold the freezes long enough for the audience to feel Keen deciding not to back away before he recommits.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: Keep Keen, the honeycomb and Fuzzby’s sleeping position readable in the same spatial relationship whenever the gag pressure builds; foreground plants may occlude but never erase the path.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: Each paw placement compresses the crunchy ground enough to prove contact; Keen’s freeze stops the whole body at once, then his reaching paw resumes with careful weight shifting toward the stump.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A repeating shape of step, CRUNCH, full-body statue, hungry glance, renewed reach; the snore bubble adds a swelling countdown over the same forbidden prize.
prohibitedStaging: Do not isolate feet, honey and face into safe inserts that lose geography.
Do not make Keen graceful or competent; his over-care is the joke.
Do not let Fuzzby’s sleep feel passive—his snore bubbles must visibly guard the honeycomb.

beats.sourceScript: A drifting speck of pollen becomes the smallest possible antagonist and beats Keen completely. His whole body tries to hold the sneeze back, making the anticipation the joke before the inevitable eruption blows his cover.

orderedEvents.text: A tiny puff of yellow pollen floats through the air… … and lands right on Keen's nose.
Beat.
Keen's nose TWITCHES. His eyes water. He tries to hold it. He holds it. He holds it. He almost stops —

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: ACHOO!

beats.whatChanges: Keen’s stealth stops being a choice and becomes a bodily inevitability; the smallest pollen speck takes control of the whole mission.
beats.whoDrives: The environment drives through the pollen; Keen drives the anticipation by trying not to sneeze instead of backing away.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits for the sneeze they know he cannot hold, enjoying the stretch before the explosion.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen tries to trap the sneeze inside his body while staying near the honeycomb, then loses the fight in one exposed ACHOO.
beats.consequence: His cover is blown; the private dare becomes public and Fuzzby can no longer remain only a sleeping obstacle.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The sneeze releases the built suspense and hands the scene to Fuzzby’s half-awake authority.

emotionContract.entryState: Over-focused and almost at the prize, believing one more act of control can save the mission.
emotionContract.pressure: A drifting pollen speck enters the exact space between Keen and the honey, and his body reacts faster than his plan can manage.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: He chooses to hold the sneeze rather than retreat, then his body proves louder than his will.
emotionContract.exitState: Exposed, startled and immediately needing to cover the failed sneak socially.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: Held breath, tightened face and body, suspended reach, then the sudden ACHOO that breaks the stealth shape.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The body has told the truth: Keen is not as controlled as his performance of bravery claimed.

comedyContract.mechanism: Anticipation to inevitable release, powered by environmental participation.
comedyContract.setup: Keen has made every sound feel dangerous and is now close enough that silence matters most.
comedyContract.expectation: He might hold himself together long enough to take the honey.
comedyContract.disruption: One tiny pollen speck beats all of his elaborate stealth technique.
comedyContract.button: The single ACHOO is bigger than every careful CRUNCH he was trying to manage.
comedyContract.hold: Hold the pre-sneeze fight just past comfort so children can predict the blast and adults can enjoy the biscuit-jar inevitability.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: Keep the pollen drifting in the space between Keen and the honeycomb, with Fuzzby still visibly asleep on the prize until the sneeze changes the room.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: Keen’s body compresses inward around the sneeze—paws braced, shoulders and muzzle tightening—before the sneeze throws his stealth posture open.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A tiny floating speck creates a whole-body pressure build, then a sudden outward burst that destroys the mission in one readable release.
prohibitedStaging: Do not cut away before the sneeze; the anticipation is the gag.
Do not make the pollen an abstract sparkle cloud; it must be one readable tiny cause.
Do not turn the sneeze into danger or gross-out; it is comic exposure.

beats.sourceScript: Fuzzby wakes just enough to defend his honeycomb with grand sleepy authority, then immediately undercuts himself by falling back into snoring. Keen is not defeated; the impossibility of the challenge makes it more interesting.

Fuzzby: Keen – No matter how hard	you try, you are never, ever, ever, ever, ever going to get my honeycomb.
Fuzzby: …ever … ZZZZZ … never zzzz … bye keen

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Fuzzby
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: Keen – No matter how hard	you try, you are never, ever, ever, ever, ever going to get my honeycomb.

beats.whatChanges: Fuzzby turns from sleeping obstacle into declared boundary, but his sleepy collapse makes the boundary comic rather than punishing; Keen reframes the warning as a bigger challenge.
beats.whoDrives: Fuzzby drives the status shift by waking and claiming the honeycomb; Keen drives the emotional turn by hearing impossibility as invitation.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience expects Keen to be in trouble, then waits to see whether Fuzzby can sustain his grand warning while still half asleep.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen awkwardly greets Fuzzby after the sneeze, Fuzzby delivers a possessive proclamation, Keen tests the words, and Fuzzby slides back into snoring mid-victory.
beats.consequence: The honey remains protected, but the contest becomes official in Keen’s mind rather than finished.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: Fuzzby’s sleepy pomp hands Keen a new dare to carry away.

emotionContract.entryState: Caught and trying to recover dignity after the sneeze.
emotionContract.pressure: Fuzzby names the failure directly by declaring the honeycomb unreachable.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: Keen chooses to focus on the size of the challenge rather than the embarrassment of being caught.
emotionContract.exitState: Curious, amused and re-energized by the word never.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: A startled greeting, attention sharpening on Fuzzby’s repeated warning, then the questioning lift in “Never … Ever?”
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: Keen has lost the honey but gained a contest he wants to revisit.

comedyContract.mechanism: Status change undercut by sleep-heavy self-importance.
comedyContract.setup: Fuzzby has been guarding the honeycomb while asleep, and the sneeze wakes him just enough to defend it.
comedyContract.expectation: His grand warning should make him fully authoritative and end the attempt.
comedyContract.disruption: His authority is thick with sleep and collapses back into snoring before the victory can stay grand.
comedyContract.button: “…ever … ZZZZZ … never zzzz … bye keen” turns the threat into a sleepy exit ramp.
comedyContract.hold: Hold the after-speech droop long enough for Fuzzby’s pomp to deflate without making him look foolishly mean.

beats.sourceScript: Keen walks away amused, carrying the challenge forward instead of losing it. The honeycomb remains untouched, which plants the promise that this little contest is not finished.
exactDialogue: Keen: We’ll see, Fuzzby. We’ll see.

orderedEvents.text: Keen walks away from the honeycomb, amused rather than defeated.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: We’ll see, Fuzzby. We’ll see.

beats.whatChanges: Keen stops pursuing the honey for now, but he keeps ownership of the game by leaving with a playful promise instead of shame.
beats.whoDrives: Keen drives the beat by choosing exit over another grab, and by turning Fuzzby’s “never” into unfinished business.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience waits to see whether the failed sneak will make Keen sulk or spark another attempt later.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen walks away amused while the honeycomb remains untouched, then answers Fuzzby’s sleepy warning with a promise to keep the challenge alive.
beats.consequence: The scene releases active suspense without resolving the contest; the untouched honeycomb becomes a standing invitation.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: Keen’s playful exit hands the scene to the witness who can reveal the failure was safe all along.

emotionContract.pressure: The prize is still there, Fuzzby has claimed it, and Keen must decide what the failed attempt means.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: He chooses to leave the honey untouched while preserving the dare for later.
emotionContract.exitState: Amused, challenged and still proud enough to come back another day.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He walks away rather than lunging again, with the line delivered as a playful promise, not a complaint.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The contest continues in spirit, and Keen’s dignity remains intact.

comedyContract.mechanism: Hiding failure by reframing defeat as strategy.
comedyContract.setup: Keen has been caught and warned that he will never get the honeycomb.
comedyContract.expectation: A failed sneak should end with disappointment or retreat.
comedyContract.disruption: Keen treats the loss as research for the next round.
comedyContract.button: “We’ll see, Fuzzby. We’ll see.” makes the untouched honey feel like a future rematch.
comedyContract.hold: Let the honeycomb sit untouched in the same calm space after the line so the audience sees that nothing was won except the game.

beats.sourceScript: Zenny reveals she has quietly witnessed the whole thing and seals the scene with one calm wink and meditative hum. Her stillness turns the earlier chaos into a shared joke.

orderedEvents.text: Nearby, ZENNY sits cross-legged on a leaf, eyes closed. As Keen recedes along the woodland path in the background, Zenny opens one eye, smiles, gives a small wink, then closes her eye again.

orderedEvents.speaker: Zenny
orderedEvents.text: OHHMMMMM…

beats.whatChanges: The supposedly private sneak is revealed as kindly witnessed; Keen’s noisy failure becomes a shared joke held in calm rather than embarrassment.
beats.whoDrives: Zenny drives the final meaning with one wink and hum, changing the scene’s allegiance from Keen’s secret mission to her quiet understanding.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience expects the scene to end on Keen’s promise, then gets the extra pleasure that someone calm saw everything and is not judging him.
beats.actionOrChoice: Zenny reveals her presence, winks and hums while the honeycomb remains untouched in warm morning calm.
beats.consequence: The nook exhales; Keen’s failed dare feels safe, affectionate and repeatable.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The final hum leaves the audience amused and warmed, carrying the honeycomb as a friendship ritual rather than a stolen prize.

emotionContract.entryState: Quietly observant and still, outside Keen’s private fantasy until the final punctuation.
emotionContract.pressure: Keen’s failure could land as embarrassment if witnessed harshly or ignored completely.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: She chooses the smallest possible response: a wink and a hum that acknowledge the whole attempt without shaming it.
emotionContract.exitState: Calm, amused and affectionate in her restraint.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: Minimal movement, one knowing wink and the steady “OHHMMMMM…” settling over the nook.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience newly understands that Keen was safe to be silly the whole time.

comedyContract.mechanism: Deadpan observation and delayed witness reveal.
comedyContract.setup: Keen behaved as if the honey mission was private, heroic and secret.
comedyContract.expectation: Only Fuzzby caught him, and the scene has already paid off with Keen’s exit line.
comedyContract.disruption: Zenny’s calm reveal shows she has understood the whole noisy attempt from stillness.
comedyContract.button: Her wink and “OHHMMMMM…” make the chaos feel tiny, fond and fully seen.
comedyContract.hold: Hold after the hum long enough for the camera’s allegiance to settle with Zenny and for the honeycomb to become calm again.

stagePlan.purpose: Turn the honeycomb from an inviting prize into a noisy private dare.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Keen begins his high-kneed tiptoe toward the honeycomb, and each careful paw placement answers with a betraying CRUNCH that freezes his whole body.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: His proud stealth routine is immediately exposed by the ground, but appetite beats caution.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: Begin embedded at nook height with the honeycomb visible as the fixed temptation; the camera creeps with Keen until the first CRUNCH interrupts its confidence and makes it stop with him.
stagePlan.observableEndState: Keen is frozen mid-approach, the honeycomb still ahead, and the path behind him visibly disturbed by crunchy ground.

stagePlan.purpose: Make Fuzzby’s sleep into an active guard system rather than passive background.
stagePlan.primaryEvent: Keen reaches toward the honey as Fuzzby sleeps on top of it, saying “ZZZZZ …”; a snore bubble swells, POPs, and Keen freezes, then the pattern repeats with the second “ZZZZZ …” as Keen inches closer.
stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The sleeping bee becomes more in charge of the mission than the awake bear.
stagePlan.cameraAndTransition: A motivated internal cut shifts from Keen’s moving stealth view to the honeycomb’s guarded depth: Keen’s reaching paw in the near path, Fuzzby on the prize, bubble growth occupying the dangerous middle space.
stagePlan.observableEndState: The second bubble has burst and Keen is closer than wisdom allows, suspended near the guarded honeycomb.

stagePlan.emotionalOrComicTurn: The private dare becomes public because Keen’s body tells the truth louder than his plan.

voicePerformances.speaker: Fuzzby
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Fuzzby: plushy, self-important little showman even in sleep; rounded, honey-thick tone with comic certainty under the drowsiness.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Unconsciously make Keen feel watched; the snore becomes a tiny guard dog for the honeycomb.
voicePerformances.subtext: This honeycomb is mine even when I am not awake enough to know I am defending it.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen, though Fuzzby is asleep and unaware.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Still asleep, but the space now feels more dangerous to Keen.
voicePerformances.pace: Slow inhale-build, then a soft trailing release on the ellipsis.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Bubble swelling rhythm: rounded, suspended, then easing down.
voicePerformances.pauses: Let a fraction of pre-roll silence catch Keen’s careful paw placement before the snore swells.
voicePerformances.breaths: Breath is the line: one sleepy nasal inhale into the Zs, tapering into the ellipsis.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Fuzzby stays planted on the honeycomb; the snore should feel bigger than his still body, stretching like a warning bubble near Keen’s freeze.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [breathes] ZZZZZ …  Direction: sleepy, full-bellied snore, not a spoken announcement; swell gently as Keen freezes, then deflate into the ellipsis.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice supports the body by making Fuzzby’s sleeping stillness feel like accidental authority.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Do not start at frame one; enter after Keen’s first careful contact, swelling through his statue-freeze and fading as hunger pulls him forward again.

voicePerformances.speaker: Fuzzby
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Fuzzby: drowsy honeycomb monarch; soft comic pomp hidden inside a snore.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Raise the pressure on Keen’s second attempt, like Fuzzby’s sleep is warning him to turn back.
voicePerformances.subtext: I am still here. Still guarding. Still extremely asleep.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen, as the trespasser Fuzzby accidentally intimidates.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Settled sleep after the first snore-pop rhythm.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Sleep gets heavier; Keen’s risk feels sillier and more doomed.
voicePerformances.pace: Even slower than the first, with more weight at the start and a lazier fall-off.
voicePerformances.rhythm: A sleepy wobble: swell, tiny catch, droop.
voicePerformances.pauses: Leave space before it so the audience feels Keen recommit; the snore interrupts that confidence.
voicePerformances.breaths: A heavier nasal draw, as if sleep is pulling Fuzzby downward while the sound rises.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Fuzzby remains asleep on the honeycomb; the bubble-swell should jolt Keen into another rigid statue, then pop him back into motion.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [breathes] ZZZZZ …  Direction: heavier and more guard-like than the first; let the Zs balloon, then sag sleepily away.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice and body tell the same joke: Fuzzby is doing nothing, yet his sleep controls Keen’s whole body.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Place after Keen’s renewed reach begins; swell long enough to force a full freeze, then release quickly into Keen’s next hungry glance.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen: eager, bright, physically overcommitted; when he tries to be quiet, the effort makes him louder.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Lose the battle with his own body; the sneeze betrays him before he can save the mission.
voicePerformances.subtext: Please, no—my sneaky plan is about to explode out of my face.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, accidentally; Keen is trying not to alert him and fails completely.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Compressed panic, holding still too hard.
voicePerformances.pace: Long silent pressure before an instant burst.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Held-in tremble, then one explosive outward hit.
voicePerformances.pauses: The important pause is before the line: hold the sneeze fight longer than comfort.
voicePerformances.breaths: A tiny trapped pre-sneeze inhale, then full release on the word.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Keen compresses around the sneeze until his stealth shape bursts open; pollen drifts after the sound.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [gasps] ACHOO!  Direction: the gasp is the final failed clamp before the sneeze; make ACHOO sudden, bright, and involuntary, not performed for attention.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice breaks the body’s attempted stillness; it should feel like the sound knocks his carefully held pose apart.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Delay until the very end of the held sneeze fight; release in one sharp outward burst with a loose tail for the follow-through.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen: quick-thinking cub energy; innocent optimism trying to outrun obvious guilt.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Recover socially and persuade Fuzzby this is normal, friendly, and definitely not a failed honeycomb theft.
voicePerformances.subtext: I have been caught, but maybe if I become cheerful fast enough, this will not count.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, newly awake and staring at him.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Awkwardly hopeful, waiting to see if charm works.
voicePerformances.pace: Sneeze is instant; the recovery is staggered and scrambling, then falsely casual on the greeting.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Burst, suspended realization, two little verbal steps, then a too-bright landing.
voicePerformances.pauses: The ellipsis is Keen seeing Fuzzby awake; hold just long enough for the social panic to arrive.
voicePerformances.breaths: After the sneeze, a small caught breath before Oh; Ah is a micro-reset into politeness.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Keen goes from burst-open sneeze to caught stiffness, then tries to assemble a friendly posture under Fuzzby’s eye-pop.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: ACHOO! … Oh, Ah, Hi Fuzzby  Direction: ACHOO involuntary; the pause is the moment Keen clocks Fuzzby. Oh is discovery, Ah is scrambling, Hi Fuzzby is over-neat and guilty-friendly.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice follows the body’s reassembly: explosion, freeze, then a carefully pasted-on greeting.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Start on the sneeze burst at the shot transition energy; let the ellipsis breathe over Fuzzby’s eye-pop before Keen’s awkward greeting lands.

voicePerformances.speaker: Fuzzby
voicePerformances.exactDialogue: Keen – No matter how hard	you try, you are never, ever, ever, ever, ever going to get my honeycomb.
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Fuzzby: grand tiny defender; theatrical certainty fighting a losing battle with sleep.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Make Keen back off by turning a sleepy possession claim into an official royal decree.
voicePerformances.subtext: I may be half-asleep, but I still need you to respect my magnificent guarding skills.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen, directly confronted at the honeycomb.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Authority wobbling downward into drowsiness, but still convinced he won.
voicePerformances.pace: Begins sharp and declarative; stretches comically through the repeated evers; slows as sleep drags at the end.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Wake-up pop, pompous decree, repetitive drumbeat of evers, then a honey-heavy final claim.
voicePerformances.pauses: Use the dash after Keen as a tiny gathering of official importance; do not pause at the tab—flow through hard you as one thought.
voicePerformances.breaths: Quick awake inhale before Keen; a small breath after try to fuel the never-ever chain.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Fuzzby snaps awake, pulls himself into a small grand guard posture, wobbles buoyantly, then begins to droop even while declaring victory.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [gasps] Keen – No matter how hard you try, you are NEVER, ever, ever, ever, ever going to get MY honeycomb.  Direction: gasp is the eye-pop wake-up; NEVER is the guard-posture flag, MY honeycomb lands as sleepy possessive pride, not meanness.

voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Enter on the sharp wake-up pop. Let the repeated evers ride the buoyant wobble, with the final honeycomb claim drooping slightly as Fuzzby sinks.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen: curiosity rebounds fast; disappointment immediately searches for a game-shaped loophole.

voicePerformances.subtext: That sounds impossible… which also sounds like something I might try later.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, as the sleepy gatekeeper of the honeycomb.
voicePerformances.pace: Small, slower than Keen’s usual speed; the second word lifts with genuine curiosity.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Drop on Never, thinking pause, upward hook on Ever.
voicePerformances.pauses: The ellipsis is Keen’s brain changing lanes from shame to challenge.
voicePerformances.breaths: Soft inhale before Never; a tiny held breath during the ellipsis as the idea turns.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Keen’s caught stiffness loosens; his focus shifts from being in trouble to understanding the rules of this future game.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: Never … EVER?  Direction: start chastened and small; let EVER brighten as the loophole appears. Do not make it defiant yet.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice matches the posture change from caught stiffness into lightened attention.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Let Fuzzby’s decree finish and droop before Keen asks; place the ellipsis over the visible moment his body unknots.

voicePerformances.speaker: Fuzzby
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Fuzzby: drowsy little emperor whose proclamation dissolves into sleep mid-sentence.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Keep winning the argument while sleep takes the microphone away.
voicePerformances.subtext: I am still guarding this… probably… good night, intruder-friend.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen, fading from direct address into dream-address.
voicePerformances.pace: Very slow and sinking; each phrase has less lift than the last.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Leftover decree fragment, snore pocket, muttered rule, snore pocket, soft farewell.
voicePerformances.pauses: Each ellipsis is a sleep-dip, not dead air; the first begins already half-submerged.

voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Fuzzby’s guard posture deflates into a quick droop and soft snoring rhythm on the honeycomb.

voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Start as Fuzzby droops from the guard pose. Let ZZZZZ align with the soft snoring rhythm; bye keen lands after the body has nearly settled.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen: buoyant challenger; kind-hearted mischief with no sting.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Claim the future rematch without taking the honeycomb now; invite Fuzzby into an ongoing game.
voicePerformances.subtext: You won today, but this just became fun.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, already drifting back to sleep.
voicePerformances.pace: Easy and measured, not rushed; he is savoring the new challenge.
voicePerformances.rhythm: First sentence to himself and Fuzzby; second sentence softer, like a promise tossed over the shoulder.
voicePerformances.pauses: The period after Fuzzby lets him choose play over grabbing; no long pause needed.
voicePerformances.breaths: Small smile-breath before the first We’ll; relaxed exhale into the final see.

voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Begin after Fuzzby’s soft bye keen has settled. Let the second sentence land as Keen is already turning or taking the first light step away.

voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Zenny: composed, airy, gently amused; minimal effort, maximum awareness.

voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Still, amused awareness from one opened eye.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Returned to peaceful stillness, with a tiny smile in the air.

direction.premise: A worried young squirrel delays leaving home for the Learning Circle until Keen’s playful curiosity and Aida’s steady honesty help him take one step at a time, where his exploding tail becomes a shared delight rather than a shameful secret.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo bring the part of himself he cannot control into a new group and discover that it is welcome there?
direction.theme: Belonging begins when you stop hiding the part of you that feels too much.
direction.externalJourney: Keen is pulled from a playful honeycomb challenge into Aida’s errand, finds Bo stuck at his doorway, walks him through the Whispering Woods, and helps him arrive at the Learning Circle, where Bo’s tail becomes the day’s favourite game.
direction.internalJourney: Bo moves from packing and unpacking as a way to avoid the unknown, to letting one new friend see his tail, then letting a whole circle celebrate it.
direction.relationshipChanges: Bo and Keen begin as stranger and helper, become co-conspirators in a tail game, and end as real friends. Aida shifts from distant seer to gentle companion, using her own admission of repeated courage to make Bo feel less alone. The bears receive Bo not by fixing him, but by asking for more of what he feared would make them reject him.
direction.emotionalCurve: Bright comic mischief opens the episode, then narrows into Bo’s doorway dread. Warmth enters through Keen’s impressed reaction, dips again on the forest log, turns on Aida’s quiet honesty and the held wind beat, then lifts into shared light, group laughter, and a sunset button that keeps the honeycomb rivalry alive.
direction.comedyCurve: Keen’s stealth is undone by pollen and sneezes; Bo’s tail turns panic into physical comedy; Sunny’s over-bright welcome is gently checked by Luna; the tail becomes a fluffy firework; Fuzzby’s final flower-disguise theft mirrors Keen’s opening attempt and pays off with Zenny’s dry, affectionate stillness.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s “never” challenge in Scene 1 return as the sunset garden button in Scene 8. Aida’s vision of Bo packing and unpacking is paid off by Bo admitting four attempts and later walking out with the satchel. Bo’s feared tail “Thing” becomes first Keen’s admiration, then a forest game, then the Learning Circle’s delight. Aida’s “every single time” becomes Bo’s courage phrase as he steps forward. Keen’s allergy to pollen becomes the practical comic bridge from honeycomb mischief to Aida’s mission.
direction.visualMotifs: Thresholds and steps: Keen tiptoeing, Bo frozen at the door, Bo taking one step then another, the path glowing forward. Expanding objects: snore bubbles, pollen puff, Bo’s tail, pink and blue light, fluffy-firework tail pops. Safe circles: honeycomb, crystal bowl, hollow tree, Learning Circle cushions, final garden wide.
direction.sonicMotifs: Crunching footsteps, snore bubbles popping, sneezes, conker/satchel rustles, the Shave-and-a-Haircut knock, repeated countdowns, tail POOFs, Aida’s rose-quartz bowl tone, Keen’s bright aquamarine note joining it, Zenny’s meditative hum as comic punctuation.
direction.climax: On the forest path, after Bo has heard that even Aida still goes every time, Aida and Keen let their crystal calls light the path; Bo chooses to step forward with them and repeats the phrase as his own action.
direction.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail is not merely tolerated; it becomes a joyful group game. Later, in golden sunset, Keen tends his garden while Fuzzby fails to steal the honeycomb, leaving the rivalry intact and the honey untouched.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, giggly belonging with a small echo of the morning challenge still unresolved: Bo is braver, Keen is kinder, and the world is still playfully unfinished.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Keen performs quietness so intensely that every betrayal becomes bigger: freeze, hungry glance, renewed reach, then a held sneeze that defeats him from inside.

contract.playableIntention: Keen believes one more act of perfect control will win the honey, but the nook keeps proving that his body and the environment are louder than his plan.

phases.observableAction: Keen advances toward the honeycomb with high knees, over-careful paw placements, a hunched stealth body, and repeated hungry looks to the prize.

Keen locks into whole-body freezes after each betrayal, then inches closer again with his paw suspended and his eyes fixed on the honeycomb.

performances.dramaticIntention: Unconsciously make Keen feel watched; the snore becomes a tiny guard dog for the honeycomb.
performances.subtext: This honeycomb is mine even when I am not awake enough to know I am defending it.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen, though Fuzzby is asleep and unaware.
performances.emotionalExit: Still asleep, but the space now feels more dangerous to Keen.
performances.pace: Slow inhale-build, then a soft trailing release on the ellipsis.
performances.rhythm: Bubble swelling rhythm: rounded, suspended, then easing down.
performances.pauses: Let a fraction of pre-roll silence catch Keen’s careful paw placement before the snore swells.
performances.breaths: Breath is the line: one sleepy nasal inhale into the Zs, tapering into the ellipsis.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Fuzzby stays planted on the honeycomb; the snore should feel bigger than his still body, stretching like a warning bubble near Keen’s freeze.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [breathes] ZZZZZ …  Direction: sleepy, full-bellied snore, not a spoken announcement; swell gently as Keen freezes, then deflate into the ellipsis.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice supports the body by making Fuzzby’s sleeping stillness feel like accidental authority.
performances.expectedTiming: Do not start at frame one; enter after Keen’s first careful contact, swelling through his statue-freeze and fading as hunger pulls him forward again.

performances.speaker: Fuzzby
performances.voiceIdentity: Fuzzby: drowsy honeycomb monarch; soft comic pomp hidden inside a snore.
performances.dramaticIntention: Raise the pressure on Keen’s second attempt, like Fuzzby’s sleep is warning him to turn back.
performances.subtext: I am still here. Still guarding. Still extremely asleep.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen, as the trespasser Fuzzby accidentally intimidates.
performances.emotionalEntry: Settled sleep after the first snore-pop rhythm.
performances.emotionalExit: Sleep gets heavier; Keen’s risk feels sillier and more doomed.
performances.pace: Even slower than the first, with more weight at the start and a lazier fall-off.
performances.rhythm: A sleepy wobble: swell, tiny catch, droop.
performances.pauses: Leave space before it so the audience feels Keen recommit; the snore interrupts that confidence.
performances.breaths: A heavier nasal draw, as if sleep is pulling Fuzzby downward while the sound rises.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Fuzzby remains asleep on the honeycomb; the bubble-swell should jolt Keen into another rigid statue, then pop him back into motion.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [breathes] ZZZZZ …  Direction: heavier and more guard-like than the first; let the Zs balloon, then sag sleepily away.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice and body tell the same joke: Fuzzby is doing nothing, yet his sleep controls Keen’s whole body.
performances.expectedTiming: Place after Keen’s renewed reach begins; swell long enough to force a full freeze, then release quickly into Keen’s next hungry glance.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: eager, bright, physically overcommitted; when he tries to be quiet, the effort makes him louder.
performances.dramaticIntention: Lose the battle with his own body; the sneeze betrays him before he can save the mission.
performances.subtext: Please, no—my sneaky plan is about to explode out of my face.
performances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, accidentally; Keen is trying not to alert him and fails completely.
performances.emotionalEntry: Compressed panic, holding still too hard.
performances.pace: Long silent pressure before an instant burst.
performances.rhythm: Held-in tremble, then one explosive outward hit.
performances.pauses: The important pause is before the line: hold the sneeze fight longer than comfort.
performances.breaths: A tiny trapped pre-sneeze inhale, then full release on the word.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen compresses around the sneeze until his stealth shape bursts open; pollen drifts after the sound.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [gasps] ACHOO!  Direction: the gasp is the final failed clamp before the sneeze; make ACHOO sudden, bright, and involuntary, not performed for attention.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice breaks the body’s attempted stillness; it should feel like the sound knocks his carefully held pose apart.
performances.expectedTiming: Delay until the very end of the held sneeze fight; release in one sharp outward burst with a loose tail for the follow-through.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: quick-thinking cub energy; innocent optimism trying to outrun obvious guilt.
performances.dramaticIntention: Recover socially and persuade Fuzzby this is normal, friendly, and definitely not a failed honeycomb theft.
performances.subtext: I have been caught, but maybe if I become cheerful fast enough, this will not count.
performances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, newly awake and staring at him.
performances.emotionalExit: Awkwardly hopeful, waiting to see if charm works.
performances.pace: Sneeze is instant; the recovery is staggered and scrambling, then falsely casual on the greeting.
performances.rhythm: Burst, suspended realization, two little verbal steps, then a too-bright landing.
performances.pauses: The ellipsis is Keen seeing Fuzzby awake; hold just long enough for the social panic to arrive.
performances.breaths: After the sneeze, a small caught breath before Oh; Ah is a micro-reset into politeness.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen goes from burst-open sneeze to caught stiffness, then tries to assemble a friendly posture under Fuzzby’s eye-pop.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: ACHOO! … Oh, Ah, Hi Fuzzby  Direction: ACHOO involuntary; the pause is the moment Keen clocks Fuzzby. Oh is discovery, Ah is scrambling, Hi Fuzzby is over-neat and guilty-friendly.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice follows the body’s reassembly: explosion, freeze, then a carefully pasted-on greeting.
performances.expectedTiming: Start on the sneeze burst at the shot transition energy; let the ellipsis breathe over Fuzzby’s eye-pop before Keen’s awkward greeting lands.

performances.speaker: Fuzzby
performances.exactDialogue: Keen – No matter how hard	you try, you are never, ever, ever, ever, ever going to get my honeycomb.
performances.voiceIdentity: Fuzzby: grand tiny defender; theatrical certainty fighting a losing battle with sleep.
performances.dramaticIntention: Make Keen back off by turning a sleepy possession claim into an official royal decree.
performances.subtext: I may be half-asleep, but I still need you to respect my magnificent guarding skills.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen, directly confronted at the honeycomb.
performances.emotionalExit: Authority wobbling downward into drowsiness, but still convinced he won.
performances.pace: Begins sharp and declarative; stretches comically through the repeated evers; slows as sleep drags at the end.
performances.rhythm: Wake-up pop, pompous decree, repetitive drumbeat of evers, then a honey-heavy final claim.
performances.pauses: Use the dash after Keen as a tiny gathering of official importance; do not pause at the tab—flow through hard you as one thought.
performances.breaths: Quick awake inhale before Keen; a small breath after try to fuel the never-ever chain.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Fuzzby snaps awake, pulls himself into a small grand guard posture, wobbles buoyantly, then begins to droop even while declaring victory.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [gasps] Keen – No matter how hard you try, you are NEVER, ever, ever, ever, ever going to get MY honeycomb.  Direction: gasp is the eye-pop wake-up; NEVER is the guard-posture flag, MY honeycomb lands as sleepy possessive pride, not meanness.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice supports the tiny grand posture but lets sleep tug at the edges, so the authority is funny rather than threatening.
performances.expectedTiming: Enter on the sharp wake-up pop. Let the repeated evers ride the buoyant wobble, with the final honeycomb claim drooping slightly as Fuzzby sinks.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: curiosity rebounds fast; disappointment immediately searches for a game-shaped loophole.
performances.dramaticIntention: Test whether Fuzzby really means forever, and quietly turn the rejection into a challenge.
performances.subtext: That sounds impossible… which also sounds like something I might try later.
performances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, as the sleepy gatekeeper of the honeycomb.
performances.pace: Small, slower than Keen’s usual speed; the second word lifts with genuine curiosity.
performances.rhythm: Drop on Never, thinking pause, upward hook on Ever.
performances.pauses: The ellipsis is Keen’s brain changing lanes from shame to challenge.
performances.breaths: Soft inhale before Never; a tiny held breath during the ellipsis as the idea turns.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen’s caught stiffness loosens; his focus shifts from being in trouble to understanding the rules of this future game.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: Never … EVER?  Direction: start chastened and small; let EVER brighten as the loophole appears. Do not make it defiant yet.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice matches the posture change from caught stiffness into lightened attention.
performances.expectedTiming: Let Fuzzby’s decree finish and droop before Keen asks; place the ellipsis over the visible moment his body unknots.

performances.speaker: Fuzzby
performances.voiceIdentity: Fuzzby: drowsy little emperor whose proclamation dissolves into sleep mid-sentence.
performances.dramaticIntention: Keep winning the argument while sleep takes the microphone away.
performances.subtext: I am still guarding this… probably… good night, intruder-friend.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen, fading from direct address into dream-address.
performances.pace: Very slow and sinking; each phrase has less lift than the last.
performances.rhythm: Leftover decree fragment, snore pocket, muttered rule, snore pocket, soft farewell.
performances.pauses: Each ellipsis is a sleep-dip, not dead air; the first begins already half-submerged.
performances.breaths: Breathy, slack consonants; ZZZZZ is fuller than the later lower-case zzzz, which should be smaller and farther away.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Fuzzby’s guard posture deflates into a quick droop and soft snoring rhythm on the honeycomb.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [quietly] …ever … ZZZZZ … never zzzz … bye keen  Direction: begin as the last crumb of authority, then let sleep swallow the line. Bye keen is affectionate and barely awake.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice collapses with the body; the authority literally melts into snoring.
performances.expectedTiming: Start as Fuzzby droops from the guard pose. Let ZZZZZ align with the soft snoring rhythm; bye keen lands after the body has nearly settled.

performances.speaker: Keen
performances.voiceIdentity: Keen: buoyant challenger; kind-hearted mischief with no sting.
performances.dramaticIntention: Claim the future rematch without taking the honeycomb now; invite Fuzzby into an ongoing game.
performances.subtext: You won today, but this just became fun.
performances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, already drifting back to sleep.
performances.pace: Easy and measured, not rushed; he is savoring the new challenge.
performances.rhythm: First sentence to himself and Fuzzby; second sentence softer, like a promise tossed over the shoulder.
performances.pauses: The period after Fuzzby lets him choose play over grabbing; no long pause needed.
performances.breaths: Small smile-breath before the first We’ll; relaxed exhale into the final see.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keen’s posture lightens and he walks away without grabbing, converting the denial into tomorrow’s game.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: We’ll SEE, Fuzzby. We’ll see.  Direction: first SEE carries playful challenge; second see is warmer and quieter, already moving away.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice supports the light walk-away energy; this is not a threat, it is Keen turning disappointment into play.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin after Fuzzby’s soft bye keen has settled. Let the second sentence land as Keen is already turning or taking the first light step away.

performances.speaker: Zenny
performances.voiceIdentity: Zenny: composed, airy, gently amused; minimal effort, maximum awareness.
performances.dramaticIntention: Seal the chaos back into calm while letting Keen know, without words, that she saw everything.
performances.subtext: Yes, I noticed. No, I do not need to make a fuss about it.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen first, then the whole nook as her hum settles the space.
performances.emotionalEntry: Still, amused awareness from one opened eye.
performances.emotionalExit: Returned to peaceful stillness, with a tiny smile in the air.
performances.pace: Unhurried, smooth, and short enough to land as a button rather than a meditation scene.
performances.rhythm: One steady hum with a faint amused lift at the front and a soft settling tail.
performances.pauses: Hold the wink before the hum just long enough for the joke to register; no internal break.
performances.breaths: Silent centered inhale before the hum; even exhale through the full sound.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Zenny opens one eye, gives the smallest amused acknowledgment, then returns to stillness as the hum settles the nook.
performances.elevenLabsV3Direction: EL text: [quietly] OHHMMMMM…  Direction: calm hum with a tiny private smile inside it; not mockery, just complete awareness.
performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice mirrors her spare movement: one eye, one tiny acknowledgment, one settling sound.
performances.expectedTiming: Do not rush in after Keen. Let the wink hold, then hum; fade into stillness as the nook calms and Fuzzby’s snore rhythm softens underneath.

beats.sourceScript: Keen turns a honeycomb into a private dare, trying to prove he can out-sneak a sleeping Fuzzby. The comedy is all body and sound: exaggerated quiet steps, betraying crunches, Fuzzby’s oblivious snore bubbles, and Keen inching closer because the prize keeps overriding caution.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.whatChanges: The honeycomb changes from an inviting prize into a guarded dare: every step announces Keen, Fuzzby’s sleeping presence becomes a living lock, and Keen’s appetite starts overriding his caution.
beats.whoDrives: Keen drives by choosing to keep advancing after each crunch and snore warning; the nook drives back through sound, texture and Fuzzby’s snore bubbles.
beats.audienceAnticipation: Children wait for the next tiny sound to betray him; adults recognize that he is much louder than he thinks and wait for the sleeping guard to notice.
beats.actionOrChoice: Keen tiptoes with exaggerated high knees, freezes after the CRUNCHes, spots and reaches for the honey, then keeps reaching as Fuzzby snores and snore bubbles grow and pop near the prize.
beats.consequence: The approach becomes more dangerous and funnier without anyone attacking him: the environment has proven that his secret mission is already noisy.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The held stealth tension hands into an even smaller threat: if crunches and snore bubbles are this loud, a speck of pollen can become enormous.
